# Give It a Twirl

> A new skirt on a tailor's dress form. Swipe sideways and it spins: the hem swings out, rises into a cone and, with a hard flick, stands out flat like a plate. Then it slows and the folds fall back one by one. Four fabrics that each move differently: chiffon, denim, a pleated mamianqun and tulle. A tiny cloth-physics toy, no sign-up.

Give It a Twirl (转圈圈 (zh-CN), Falda con Vuelo (es), La Jupe qui Tourne (fr), くるくるスカート (ja)) is a free browser toy at https://twirl.integ.life/ by Integ Life. It opens straight into play: no sign-up, no download, no ads, no tutorial. It works with a mouse or a touchscreen on phones, tablets and computers.

## How to play

1. Swipe sideways anywhere, with a finger or the mouse. The dress form turns on its stand like a wheel and keeps the speed you gave it.
2. Below about one turn a second the skirt only swings. Faster, and the hem lifts; at two turns a second it stands out flat. Swipe again to keep it there.
3. Hold a finger still on it to brake. The form stops; the skirt keeps going and wraps round it.
4. Tap a hanger at the top to change the skirt: chiffon, denim, a pleated mamianqun or tulle. Each one flies differently.

## Facts

- URL: https://twirl.integ.life/
- Price: free
- Platforms: any modern web browser (desktop and mobile)
- Languages: English, 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese), Español, Français and 日本語 (Japanese), picked from the browser language (default English)
- Sound: synthesised live with the Web Audio API; vibration on Android
- Made by: Integ Life (https://integ.life/), first published 2026-11-26

## FAQ

**Why does the skirt rise when it spins?**
Every bit of cloth is trying to go in a straight line while the waist pulls it round in a circle, so the cloth swings outward, and the faster it goes the higher it rises. A strip 62 cm long starts to lift at about 0.8 turns a second and is nearly level at 2. The toy simulates the cloth and lets this happen by itself.

**What is a mamianqun?**
A traditional Chinese pleated skirt (马面裙, 'horse-face skirt'). It is made of flat front and back panels with pressed knife pleats between them. When it spins the pleats fan open into a bell and the flat panels stay flat.

**Is there anyone wearing the skirt?**
No. It is on a tailor's dress form, a linen torso on an iron stand.

**Why did things fly out of the denim skirt?**
It has pockets.

**Is Give It a Twirl free?**
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up, no download and no ads. It runs in any modern browser on phones, tablets and computers.

**Does it have sound and vibration?**
Yes. The rush of the cloth, the tick of the stand and a small note for every full turn are synthesised live with the Web Audio API; there are no audio files. On Android phones each quarter turn is also a tick of vibration.

**Which languages does it support?**
English, 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese), Español, Français and 日本語 (Japanese). The language is picked automatically from your browser settings; any other language falls back to English.

**Who made it?**
Integ Life (integ.life). Give It a Twirl is one of eleven small stress-relief toys, together with Charge Burst, Void Harvest, Glass Smash, Chain Pop, Knock on Wood, Lap Cat, Squishy Bun, Scratch That, Peel Off, Tablecloth Trick. More games are at games.integ.life.

**Is any personal data collected?**
No account and no personal data. At most, anonymous usage statistics (page views and play counts) are collected.
